description: With pre-compute-only embedding (no live embedder), the HybridIndex cannot embed search queries for vector search. Two options to resolve: Option A (recommended) — fall back to BM25-only when no embedder is configured; HybridIndex.Search detects nil/stub embedder and skips vector ranking, returns BM25 results only. Option B — spawn a Python subprocess to embed a single query string and return binary float32 to stdout; acceptable if query latency ~500ms is tolerable. Decision affects: internal/search/hybrid.go (nil embedder guard), cmd/shuttle/main.go (embedder config), and whether Option B requires a minimal embed_query.py script. Resolve this before implementing the HNSW vector index.
title: Decide query-time vector search strategy

description:
Research and plan which local ASR model to use for the transcriber (replacing StubTranscriber), given M1 Air with 8GB RAM. Must run entirely locally — no API calls.

The transcriber receives an audio file path and must return speaker-diarized TranscriptSegment slices (SpeakerID, StartMs, EndMs, Text). The Transcriber interface is already defined in internal/ingest/transcribe.go.

## Hardware constraint
- Apple Silicon M1 Air, 8GB unified memory
- MLX already installed and working
- Python available

## Models to evaluate

### Transcription
- **mlx-whisper (large-v3)** — Apple MLX port of Whisper, runs natively on M1 Neural Engine. Best quality, ~3GB. Recommended starting point given MLX is already in use.
- **mlx-whisper (medium / small)** — faster, less accurate, ~1.5GB / ~500MB
- **faster-whisper (large-v3, int8)** — CTranslate2 backend, CPU+CoreML, ~2GB, no MLX dependency
- **whisper.cpp** — pure C++, CoreML acceleration, ~1-3GB depending on model size

### Speaker diarization (separate from transcription)
- **pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1** — requires HuggingFace token, ~500MB, runs on CPU/MPS
- **nemo-msdd** — NVIDIA NeMo, heavier dependency
- **simple-diarizer** — lightweight, less accurate but no auth needed
- Note: diarization is optional for MVP; can ship without it and add later

## Deliverable
Decision record specifying:
1. Chosen transcription model + backend (MLX vs faster-whisper vs whisper.cpp)
2. Whether to include diarization in v1 or defer it
3. How Go calls the transcriber: subprocess (like embed.py pattern) or REST
4. Go interface plan: how upload_handler.go calls the local transcriber

No implementation yet — planning only.
title: Plan local ASR transcriber (M1 Air, 8GB)

description:
Add a --convert subcommand to python/embed.py that reads one or more existing .embed TSV files (columns: file_name, start_token, embedding, text) and writes them as .fembed binary files without re-running the model.

Usage: python embed.py --convert --embed-file foo.embed [--out-file foo.fembed]
       python embed.py --convert --embed-dir ./embeddings/  (batch convert *.embed in dir)

Implementation:
- Parse the TSV with csv.reader (tab delimiter), skip header row
- For each row: source_file=col[0], start_token=int(col[1]), embedding=[float(x) for x in col[2].split(',')], text=col[3]
- Detect dims from first row's embedding length
- Call write_fembed() with the collected records (already implemented)
- Default output: same path with .fembed extension replacing .embed

Edge cases: handle csv.field_size_limit (already set), skip empty rows, validate header, warn on dim mismatch across rows.

This enables zero-recompute migration of existing .embed files to the binary format for ingestion via POST /api/v1/ingest/embed-file.
title: Add .embed TSV → .fembed converter to embed.py

description:
One-time operational task: convert and load all existing .embed TSV files into the SQLite store and HNSW index.

Prerequisites: flying-shuttle-7p6 (Python converter) OR flying-shuttle-vv9 (Go native import) must be complete.

Recommended path once vv9 is done (no Python needed):
  curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ingest/embed-file-legacy     -H 'Content-Type: application/json'     -d '{"path": "/absolute/path/to/file.embed"}'

Or batch via directory (requires .fembed conversion first):
  python embed.py --convert --embed-dir ./embeddings/
  curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ingest/directory     -d '{"path": "/absolute/path/to/embeddings"}'

Verification:
- Check SQLite: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(embedding_vec) FROM chunks;
  → COUNT(*) should equal number of records in .embed file(s)
  → COUNT(embedding_vec) should equal COUNT(*) (all chunks have vectors)
- Check HNSW: server log should show 'loaded HNSW index from shuttle.hnsw (N vectors)' on restart
- Test search: POST /api/v1/search?q=<term> should return results
title: Ingest existing .embed files into system

description:
Add a Go reader for the legacy .embed TSV format so existing files can be ingested directly via the API without a Python conversion step.

New file: internal/ingest/embedfile/tsv_reader.go

type TSVReader struct { ... }
func OpenTSV(path string) (*TSVReader, error)  // opens and validates header
func (r *TSVReader) Next() (*Record, error)    // reuses same Record type as .fembed reader
func (r *TSVReader) Close() error

Implementation:
- Use encoding/csv with tab delimiter and csv.LazyQuotes=true
- Read and validate header row: [file_name, start_token, embedding, text]
- Per row: parse start_token as int32, split embedding column on ',' and parse each float32
- Return Record{SourceFile, StartToken, Text, Embedding} — same type as fembed.Record
- Dims() returns len of first parsed embedding (detected at runtime, not from header)

New API endpoint: POST /api/v1/ingest/embed-file-legacy
  Body: {"path": "/absolute/path/to/file.embed"}
  Handler: same logic as importEmbedFile but uses TSVReader instead of fembed.Reader

Wire into router.go under /api/v1/ingest/embed-file-legacy.

Benefit: users with existing .embed files can ingest without running Python at all. The TSV float parsing is the only overhead vs .fembed.
title: Add native Go .embed TSV importer (no Python required)

description:
Now that Qwen3 embeddings can be imported via the ingest API, verify that the full hybrid search pipeline works end-to-end and tune it for good results.

Scope:
1. Confirm chunks imported from .fembed files are indexed in BOTH BM25 (HybridIndex.BM25) and HNSW (HybridIndex.Vector) — already wired in IndexChunks(), but needs smoke-test with real data.

2. Add search mode param to GET /api/v1/search:
   ?mode=hybrid (default) — RRF fusion of BM25 + HNSW vector results
   ?mode=bm25   — BM25 only (current query-time behaviour since embedder=nil)
   ?mode=vector — HNSW only (requires pre-computed query vector; skip for now or 501)
   This makes the mode explicit and testable without changing default behaviour.

3. Tune RRF k constant: current default k=60 was chosen for general use. With Qwen3 2560-dim vectors and the specific transcript-chunk domain, k may need adjustment. Add SHUTTLE_RRF_K env var (default 60) so it can be tuned at runtime without recompile.

4. Add ?limit param to search endpoint (currently hardcoded to 10 in handler). Surface it as a query param with a sensible max cap (e.g. 100).

Acceptance: after importing a .fembed file, a BM25 query for a keyword known to be in a chunk returns that chunk, AND (once vector index is populated) an HNSW-adjacent chunk also surfaces via the hybrid mode.
title: Verify and tune hybrid BM25+Qwen3 search after ingest
